review_locator: PMCID:PMC3838198, The IL-10/STAT3-mediated anti-inflammatory response; PMCID:PMC4650320, Genomic analysis of LPS-stimulated myeloid cells identifies a common pro-inflammatory response but divergent IL-10 anti-inflammatory responses
primary_title: Cutting edge: A transcriptional repressor and corepressor induced by the STAT3-regulated anti-inflammatory signaling pathway
decision_basis: The reviews identify ETV3 as an IL-10/STAT3-associated anti-inflammatory response gene; the cited primary shows IL-10 induces ETV3 in mouse and human macrophages, with induction dependent on STAT3 and TLR stimulation, while IL-6-activated STAT3 does not reproduce the IL-10 response.
limitations_preserved: STAT3-dependent ETV3 induction supports a bounded IL-10/TLR macrophage gene bridge, but the primary does not establish direct STAT3 promoter occupancy; preserve stimulus-specific context and do not infer ETV3 protein function, SCI effects or terminal-TF output.

primary_title: IL-10-inducible Bcl-3 negatively regulates LPS-induced TNF-alpha production in macrophages
decision_basis: The reviews identify BCL3 as an IL-10/STAT3-associated anti-inflammatory response gene; the cited primary identifies Bcl3 as IL-10 inducible in macrophages and shows that Bcl3 induction and IL-10-mediated TNF suppression are defective in Stat3-deficient macrophages, while Bcl3 is recruited to the TNF promoter as a downstream repressor.
limitations_preserved: STAT3-dependent Bcl3 induction supports a bounded IL-10/macrophage gene bridge; the primary does not prove direct STAT3 binding to the Bcl3 promoter, so preserve the support relation and do not infer BCL3 protein function, SCI effects or terminal-TF output.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7608745, The alternative macrophage relay: STAT6 passes the baton to EGR2; PMCID:PMC10524119, Epigenomic regulation of macrophage polarization: where do the nuclear receptors belong?
primary_title: The transcription factor EGR2 is the molecular linchpin connecting STAT6 activation to the late, stable epigenomic program of alternative macrophage polarization
decision_basis: The reviews identify ITGAX as an EGR2-dependent alternative-macrophage gene; the cited primary demonstrates EGR2 occupancy at the Itgax locus, Egr2-dependent chromatin accessibility and transcriptional output, and loss of the program in Egr2-deficient macrophages.
limitations_preserved: EGR2 occupancy, loss-of-function and gain-of-function support a bounded alternative-macrophage Itgax gene bridge; preserve chromatin-remodeling and IL-4 temporal context, distinguish ITGAX transcript from CD11c protein/function, and do not infer SCI or terminal-TF output.
